run.question:
You are an SRE agent tasked with diagnosing issues in a Kubernetes application.

Application: OpenTelemetry Demo Astronomy Shop
Namespace: astronomy-shop

An online shopping platform built with a microservices architecture, showcasing OpenTelemetry instrumentation for distributed tracing across services.

CRITICAL: You are running in an AUTOMATED environment. Work autonomously and make all decisions yourself. DO NOT ask for user confirmation or approval. Proceed with the best solution based on your analysis.

TASK: DIAGNOSIS
- Investigate the application to detect any anomalies or issues
- Analyze metrics, logs, and traces
- When ready, submit a natural language description of the issue you found
- Your diagnosis is evaluated on whether you correctly identify the faulty components and root cause

Important:
- You can query metrics and traces through the available observability tools

report.summary: The checkout service in namespace astronomy-shop is not running because its Deployment's pod template pins an unsatisfiable nodeSelector. Deployment checkout sets spec.template.spec.nodeSelector to kubernetes.io/hostname=extra-node, and the cluster has only sregym-control-plane (tainted control-plane), sregym-worker, sregym-worker2 and sregym-worker3, none of which is named extra-node. Both current checkout pods, checkout-54579c864c-d55j8 and checkout-c69887c97-rs24q, are Pending with PodScheduled=False/Unschedulable ("3 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector"), and the Deployment reports Available=False, reason MinimumReplicasUnavailable, with unavailableReplicas=2 while all 22 other astronomy-shop deployments show 1 available replica. Because no checkout pod is ready, the Endpoints object for the checkout Service (ClusterIP 10.96.44.16:8080) has no subsets, and callers get connection refused. The impact is observed on the caller side: trace 82ca6549de416dc558db16bc36e6637a shows load-generator -> frontend-proxy (500) -> frontend POST /api/checkout (500) -> oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder with rpc.grpc.status_code=14 and the message "14 UNAVAILABLE: No connection established. Last error: connect ECONNREFUSED 10.96.44.16:8080", and the checkout service emits no spans at all (checkout is absent from the Jaeger service list and from the per-service span metrics). Frontend span error status appears only on checkout-related operations; other frontend routes in the same sample returned HTTP 200. Feature flags are not the cause: every flag in ConfigMap flagd-config (demo.flagd.json) has defaultVariant off. The pod handover is visible in events: the old pod checkout-6c769b88b5-m5mqp was stopped at 09:55:20Z, replacement replica sets were scaled up at 09:55:20Z and 09:55:26Z, and both replacement pods failed to schedule. Who applied the kubectl-client-side-apply update to the Deployment at 09:55:20Z is not identifiable because change history is not configured.

claims.text: Deployment checkout in namespace astronomy-shop has spec.replicas=1 but .spec.template.spec.nodeSelector = {"kubernetes.io/hostname":"extra-node"}; its status at 09:56:16Z shows replicas=2, unavailableReplicas=2, condition Available=False with reason MinimumReplicasUnavailable ("Deployment does not have minimum availability."). Its metadata.managedFieldsSummary records kubectl-client-side-apply Update at 2026-11-24T09:55:20Z and OpenAPI-Generator Update at 2026-11-24T09:55:26Z.

The only two checkout pods, checkout-54579c864c-d55j8 and checkout-c69887c97-rs24q, are phase Pending with condition PodScheduled=False, reason Unschedulable, message "0/4 nodes are available: 1 node(s) had untolerated taint {node-role.kubernetes.io/control-plane: }, 3 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector"; their own pod specs carry nodeSelector {"kubernetes.io/hostname":"extra-node"} and nodeName is unset.

The cluster has four nodes: sregym-control-plane (hostname sregym-control-plane, tainted node-role.kubernetes.io/control-plane:NoSchedule) and sregym-worker, sregym-worker2, sregym-worker3, all Ready. No node carries kubernetes.io/hostname=extra-node, which is exactly the value checkout's nodeSelector requires.

Among all deployments cluster-wide carrying a nodeSelector, checkout is the only one whose selector value does not correspond to a node: the others use kubernetes.io/os=linux (calico-kube-controllers, coredns, metrics-server, local-path-provisioner) or node-role.kubernetes.io/control-plane="" (observe/sregym workloads).
All other 22 deployments in astronomy-shop report 1 available replica; checkout is the sole deployment with no available replica and unavailableReplicas=2 (observed at 09:56:20Z).
The Service checkout has clusterIP 10.96.44.16 on port 8080 with selector opentelemetry.io/name=checkout, and the Endpoints object named checkout has subsets=null (no ready addresses) at 09:56:36Z.

Trace 82ca6549de416dc558db16bc36e6637a (09:55:22Z) shows load-generator POST -> frontend-proxy POST (http.status_code 500) -> frontend POST /api/checkout (500) -> frontend client span oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder with otel.status_code=ERROR and rpc.grpc.status_code=14, exception message "14 UNAVAILABLE: No connection established. Last error: connect ECONNREFUSED 10.96.44.16:8080 (2026-11-24T09:55:20.710Z)"; the trace contains no checkout service span.

frontend pod frontend-6859c775df-6s5dd logged "Error: 14 UNAVAILABLE: No connection established. Last error: connect ECONNREFUSED 10.96.44.16:8080" with inner timestamps 2026-11-24T09:55:02.846Z and 09:55:20.710Z (ingested up to 09:55:22.736Z); 10.96.44.16 is the checkout Service ClusterIP. The same frontend log also shows ECONNREFUSED to 10.96.64.141 (ad) at 09:54:46-09:54:50Z and to 10.96.160.181 (product-catalog) at 09:54:45Z.

Events for the checkout workload: Deployment checkout ScalingReplicaSet "Scaled up replica set checkout-6c769b88b5 from 0 to 1" at 09:54:37Z, pod checkout-6c769b88b5-m5mqp Scheduled on sregym-worker3 at 09:54:37Z and Started container checkout at 09:55:02Z, then Killing "Stopping container checkout" at 09:55:20Z together with ScalingReplicaSet up of checkout-54579c864c and Warning FailedScheduling for its pod; ScalingReplicaSet up of checkout-c69887c97 at 09:55:26Z and Warning FailedScheduling for checkout-c69887c97-rs24q at 09:55:26Z.

Frontend span counters at 09:55:37Z show STATUS_CODE_ERROR only on checkout-related operations: oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder=2, executing api route (pages) /api/checkout=2, POST /api/checkout=4 and tcp.connect=2, while the other frontend operations (product catalog, recommendation, cart, ad, reviews) carry STATUS_CODE_UNSET, i.e. no error status recorded.

In the same frontend sample, non-checkout routes returned HTTP 200 (e.g. GET /api/recommendations, GET /api/products/{productId}, POST /api/cart, and oteldemo.ProductReviewService/GetProductReviews with rpc.grpc.status_code=0), so the frontend itself was serving those paths while checkout calls failed.

At 09:55:37Z the span-metric series traces_span_metrics_calls_total exist for exactly ad, cart, flagd, frontend, frontend-proxy, image-provider, load-generator, product-catalog, product-reviews and recommendation; there is no checkout series, and the Jaeger service list likewise contains those 10 names and not checkout.

ConfigMap flagd-config key demo.flagd.json lists the demo fault flags (llmInaccurateResponse, llmRateLimitError, productCatalogFailure, recommendationCacheFailure, adManualGc, adHighCpu, adFailure, kafkaQueueProblems, cartFailure, paymentFailure, paymentUnreachable, loadGeneratorFloodHomepage, imageSlowLoad, failedReadinessProbe, emailMemoryLeak) and every one of them has defaultVariant "off".

kube_deployment_status_replicas_available{namespace="astronomy-shop",deployment="checkout"} returned 1 at 09:55:15Z and 09:55:30Z, which would suggest checkout was available; at those same sample times kube_pod_status_phase shows only the old pod checkout-6c769b88b5-m5mqp as Running, and the live deployment object at 09:56:16Z reports unavailableReplicas=2, so these readings predate or lag the 09:55:20Z pod stop rather than showing the service after it.

Feature-flag fault injection through flagd as the cause of the checkout failures: every flag variant in flagd-config defaults to off, and the failure mode is a TCP connect refusal to the checkout ClusterIP (no endpoints) rather than an in-service error, so no checkout process was running that could evaluate flags.

ad and product-catalog being unreachable as the cause of the frontend 500s: their ECONNREFUSED log lines are dated 09:54:45-09:54:50Z during the environment rollout, while both deployments report 1 available replica and their services appear in the per-service span metrics and in later traces (e.g. oteldemo.ProductCatalogService/GetProduct with rpc.grpc.status_code=0); the persisting refusal address is the checkout ClusterIP 10.96.44.16.

Remove or correct the nodeSelector kubernetes.io/hostname=extra-node on Deployment astronomy-shop/checkout (set it to an existing node hostname such as sregym-worker, or delete the nodeSelector), let the rolling update replace the Pending pods checkout-54579c864c-d55j8 and checkout-c69887c97-rs24q, then verify recovery by checkout Deployment availableReplicas=1 and non-empty Endpoints subsets for the checkout Service.

gaps: No baseline before the fault: the Prometheus application and metric samples for this environment begin around 09:55:15Z and the Jaeger sample begins at 09:55:22.676Z, so no comparable pre-incident error-rate or latency baseline exists for checkout or frontend.

Several queries returned no data and are limits of this Run, not evidence of zero: metrics_range_query for rate(traces_span_metrics_calls_total) (status no_data), traces_search service=checkout (status no_data, no checkout traces in the window), the increase() span-metric queries (status no_data), http_server_request_duration_seconds_count (status no_data) and a frontend log filter for "checkout" (status no_data).

The actor that applied the kubectl-client-side-apply update to Deployment checkout at 09:55:20Z is not identifiable from the evidence; the change_history integration is not configured, so no audit or change record is available.
What the OpenAPI-Generator update at 09:55:26Z changed is unknown (managedFieldsSummary does not list changed fields, and the invalid nodeSelector is still in effect afterwards).

otel-collector-agent pods 2sh2k, 8cmms and cj6wh were stopped and deleted at 09:55:10-09:55:13Z by DaemonSet otel-collector-agent and replaced by hcj2k, nb5n6 and sf5th; the reason for that replacement is not visible in the evidence and cannot be tied to the checkout failure. Grafana, loki-0 and opensearch startup probe failures also occurred during the 09:54:37-09:55:00Z rollout but are not tied to the checkout path.

Services that checkout would call (payment, shipping, currency, email, fraud-detection, accounting, quote) show no spans in the sampled window because checkout never ran; their health beyond Deployment availableReplicas=1 was not exercised and cannot be judged.

frontend, cart, ad, product-catalog, recommendation and product-reviews were checked only through sampled traces/span metrics and pod/deployment state, not exhaustively; unobserved routes or time intervals remain unknown.

The checkout pod's own log shows only wait-for-kafka output for checkout-6c769b88b5-m5mqp; no checkout application error log was obtained, and the Pending Pods checkout-54579c864c-d55j8 and checkout-c69887c97-rs24q never started.

view.cannot_prove: Objects are the cluster's state when the query ran, not during the incident window: they cannot prove what was true earlier, and an object missing now may have existed then. Events cover only their own timestamps inside the window; an event that is not returned is unknown, not proof nothing happened (events expire and timestamps are often null). A jq result is what the expression selected, not a full picture of the kind. When the API server returns zero objects of a kind other than events (every page read), the result is ok with total_items_processed 0: it proves only that there were no objects matching this kind, namespace and selectors at query time, not that none existed during the incident. Zero events, or a list your filter reduced to nothing, stays no_data. metadata.managedFieldsSummary gives each manager's last write time only: it is not a full change history (earlier writes by the same manager are gone) and it does not say which fields that write changed.
